title: 2.2.11 Collectible Class
description: Write a Collectible class, instantiate at least 5, and detect overlap with the player. SLO-2 lab — the class is the point.

steps.title: Define the Collectible class
steps.instructions: Write `class Collectible { }` with a `constructor(x, y, value, color)`. Store `x`, `y`, and `value` on `this`. Create `this.sprite = new Sprite(x, y, 20, 20)` and set its color.
hints: Inside the constructor, `this` refers to the new object being built.
Sprite size is up to you — 15-25 works well.

steps.title: Add a collect() method
steps.instructions: Add a `collect()` method on the class that calls `this.sprite.remove()` and returns `this.value`.
hints: Method syntax: `collect() { ... }` — no `function` keyword inside a class.

steps.title: Instantiate at least 5 Collectibles
steps.instructions: In `setup()` (after the player is created), push at least 5 `new Collectible(...)` into the `collectibles` array at different positions. Give them different values and colors.
hints: Use a loop if you want: `for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { collectibles.push(new Collectible(...)); }`

steps.title: Detect overlaps and collect
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, iterate the `collectibles` array. If `player.overlaps(c.sprite)`, call `c.collect()`, add the return value to `totalScore`, and remove that item from the array.
hints: Iterate backwards when removing during iteration: `for (let i = collectibles.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)`.

requirements.title: collect() method
requirements.description: A collect method exists in the class.

requirements.title: At least one instance
requirements.description: At least one Collectible is instantiated.

requirements.title: Overlap detection
requirements.description: The code checks for overlap between player and a sprite.
